headline: GOLD POSTS WORST WEEK IN SIX — $3,984 Close, Down 3.4%; Iran Strikes Drive Oil +11%, Revive Rate Hike Bets
snippet: Gold fell 3.4% this week — its biggest weekly loss in six — closing Friday around $3,984 as U.S. military strikes on Iran drove oil prices up 11%, stoking inflation fears and reviving the case for Federal Reserve rate hikes that compress the non-yielding metal. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to price stability even as softer June CPI 'largely ruled out a July hike,' leaving September live; silver shed nearly 7% for the week as its industrial demand profile made it doubly vulnerable to the growth-slowdown/inflation pincer.

headline: LI-FT POWER KICKS OFF 163-HOLE QUEBEC LITHIUM DRILL — 38,970m at Adina-Galinée; 4 James Bay Properties Active (TSXV:LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power (TSXV: LIFT) announced today the commencement of drilling at its Adina-Galinée Lithium Project in Québec, launching a 163-hole, 38,970-metre campaign simultaneously across four James Bay Belt properties — AGLP, Cancet, Tilly, and Nottaway-Sirmac-Clapier. The AGLP sits in the same emerging hard-rock lithium district as Patriot Battery Metals' Corvette discovery and Winsome Resources' Adina project; the 2026 program is designed to advance resource definition while expanding the land position along one of North America's most active lithium belts.

headline: ASX GOLD SUB-INDEX BLEEDS 6.5% THIS WEEK — Worst Since March; Ora Banda -7%, Evolution -4%, NST -4% on Iran Oil Shock
snippet: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 Gold Sub-Index (XGD) fell 4.9% on Friday and lost 6.5% for the week — its worst weekly performance since mid-March 2026 — as the US-Iran conflict's oil price surge revived fears of sustained inflation and Federal Reserve rate hikes. Ora Banda Mining led declines at -7.4%, followed by Emerald Resources (-4.8%), Evolution Mining (-4.3%), and Northern Star (-4.1%); the broader ASX 200 materials index dropped 2.9% on Friday, with BHP and Rio each losing over 2% as copper and lithium names were also sold.

headline: GENESIS EATS VAULT IN A$12.6BN DEAL — Australia's Third Gold Producer Born; 700K oz/yr, A$2B Synergies, November Close (ASX:GMD/VAU)
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) and Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) agreed to merge via scheme of arrangement, valuing Vault at A$5.274 per share — a 15.7% premium — to create a combined enterprise worth approximately A$12.6 billion targeting 600,000–700,000 oz/yr from Western Australia's Leonora and Bardoc-Mount Monger districts. The new entity ranks as Australia's third-largest listed gold producer by market cap, formed after rival bidder Regis Resources withdrew; A$2 billion in operational synergies are projected from the close proximity of operations, with deal completion targeted for November 2026.

headline: ANTOFAGASTA H1 COPPER -9.5% — 285K Tonnes as Los Pelambres and Centinela Both Underperform; 650K–700K Full-Year Guidance Intact
snippet: Antofagasta (LON: ANTO) reported H1 2026 copper production of 285,000 tonnes, a 9.5% year-on-year decline, as lower processing rates and ore grades at its flagship Los Pelambres and Centinela concentrators both fell short of prior-year levels. Q2 output of 142,000 tonnes was down just 1% quarter-on-quarter, an early sign of stabilisation; the company maintained its 2026 full-year guidance of 650,000–700,000 tonnes — with results released the same week a powerful atmospheric river struck Chile's copper-producing regions, adding fresh H2 supply risk.

headline: CAMECO'S CIGAR LAKE BACK ONLINE — Acid Plant Fixed After Two-Week Shutdown; 17.5M–18M lb 2026 Uranium Guidance Unchanged (TSX:CCO)
snippet: Cameco (TSX: CCO / NYSE: CCJ) confirmed July 14 that Cigar Lake has resumed production following a two-week stoppage triggered by a sulfuric acid plant failure at Orano's McClean Lake mill — the only facility that processes Cigar Lake ore. The mine resumed shipping stockpiled ore once Orano completed repairs and restored milling; Cameco's 2026 Cigar Lake guidance of 17.5–18.0 million pounds U3O8 (100% basis) was unchanged, with the root cause traced to Strait of Hormuz disruptions and Chinese sulphuric acid export restrictions cutting global supply.

headline: WALLBRIDGE MARTINIERE EXPANDS BUG LAKE CORRIDOR — 36.10 g/t Peak, 4.34 g/t Over 10m; Phase 2 Paused by Fires (TSX:WM)
snippet: Wallbridge Mining (TSX: WM) released Phase 1 results from the Bug Lake deformation corridor at its 100%-owned Martiniere gold project in Québec's Abitibi Greenstone Belt, with six holes (4,108 metres) intersecting multiple gold-bearing shear structures — highlights include 36.10 g/t Au over 0.5 metres, 4.34 g/t Au over 10.0 metres, and 2.63 g/t Au over 9.8 metres across five of the six holes. Phase 2 drilling, originally planned for early July, has been temporarily postponed due to nearby forest fires; the Bug Lake corridor hosts the majority of the Martiniere NI 43-101 mineral resource.

headline: OREZONE 58,566 oz Q2 — First Full Quarter as Two-Mine Producer; Bomboré and Casa Berardi Both on Guidance Track (TSX/ASX:ORE)
snippet: Orezone Gold (TSX/ASX: ORE) delivered consolidated Q2 2026 gold production of 58,566 ounces — bringing H1 2026 to 97,355 oz — in its first full quarter as a multi-mine producer after acquiring Casa Berardi from Endeavour Mining. Bomboré in Burkina Faso exceeded its quarterly ore-tonnes plan, while Casa Berardi in Ontario advanced underground development and definition drilling to support higher future throughput; full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed with Q2 financial results due August 12.

headline: KUTCHO COPPER DRILLS FIRST NEW TARGETS IN 15 YEARS — 2 Rigs Hit Hamburger, Gap and Esso West in B.C.'s Stikine (TSXV:KC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Kutcho Copper Corp.
snippet: Kutcho Copper Corp. (TSX-V: KC) launched its 2026 drill campaign with two rigs at the feasibility-stage Kutcho copper-zinc project in northwest British Columbia's Stikine Terrane on July 14 — the first comprehensive exploration program to test multiple new targets on the property in over 15 years. The two rigs will sequentially test the Hamburger, Gap, and Esso West zones adjacent to the existing NI 43-101 resource, with results expected to inform a potential resource expansion and feed into a future feasibility update.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: GOLD'S CASE INTACT AT $4,000 — Iran Pullback Is Structural Noise; Central Bank Buying and Miner Margins Underpin
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 outlook argues that gold's ~28% pullback from its January $5,589 peak to $4,000 mirrors prior bull market corrections and does not invalidate the structural thesis: central bank accumulation is intact (45% of central banks plan to increase gold holdings), miner all-in sustaining costs remain well below $2,000/oz even at current prices, and the Iran geopolitical premium is sitting in oil — not gold — temporarily. The piece positions the current zone as matching the 'demand vacuum' pattern from gold's four prior major pullbacks between 2020 and 2026.

headline: GOLDSEEK: BULLS VS. BEARS ON GOLD'S WAR NARRATIVE — Does the Iran Escalation Help or Hurt the Metal From $4,000?
snippet: GoldSeek examines why gold has fallen despite escalating US-Iran military conflict — defying the traditional safe-haven playbook. The bull case holds that the Iran risk is transitory and gold's structural drivers remain intact; the bear case argues the oil price spike translates directly into inflation and Federal Reserve rate hikes that suppress gold via real yield expansion. The piece notes that junior and mid-tier miners with lower all-in sustaining costs have held up better than large-cap producers in the current drawdown, and flags the July 28-29 FOMC meeting as the next binary event.
